newsitem.title: JAPAN: Shiseido says aims to be in top 3 cosmetics firms.
newsitem.headline: Shiseido says aims to be in top 3 cosmetics firms.

text.p: Shiseido Co Ltd aims to be one of the world's top three cosmetics firms by 2005, director Yasutaka Mori said on Tuesday.

It hopes to reach this position after completing a five-year globalisation plan that aims to boost annual group net sales to 800 billion yen, a quarter of it coming from overseas sales, by the turn of the century, said Mori in an interview.
The current top three firms in the cosmetics industry are the L'Oreal Group, Procter & Gamble Co and Unilever. Shiseido is ranked fourth.

As part of Shiseido's globalisation plans, the firm has started expanding its overseas businesses aggressively. Last year it purchased Helene Curtis Industries Inc's assets in the hair salon business.
Shiseido is also planning to launch new products targeted solely at the international market, such as a new skincare and makeup brand called "Za", to be launched on September 1.
"We hope to complete introducing new brands by the year 1999, although we have no time limit for mergers," said Mori, who is also chief officer of Shiseido's international headquarters.
